of the longest-tenured coaches in the Mid-American Conference, Rob Marinaro has been part of the Kent State’s women’s soccer staff since the program’s inception in 1997 and is in his 25th season as head coach of the Golden Flashes.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>The three-time MAC Coach of the Year has the second-most wins in conference history and owns a 255-217-61 record, including a 148-121-33 mark in league play. Marinaro has led Kent State to one MAC Tournament championship, three MAC regular season titles and three MAC East Division crowns during his tenure. Additionally, he has overseen the development of two All-Americans, 14 All-Region honorees and 48 All-MAC selections. In 2018, Marinaro captured the 200th win in school history and earned his 200th win at the helm of the program against Bowling Green in 2022.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>The success does not end on the field for Marinaro’s teams, as the women’s soccer team regularly posts one of Kent State Athletics’ highest term grade-point averages. The Flashes have been among the nation’s elite academically as noted by 10 NSCAA Team Academic Awards since 2007, which included a national Top-20 GPA for four consecutive seasons from 2009-12. Marinaro’s student-athletes have earned three CoSIDA Academic All-American honors, 28 MAC Distinguished Scholar-Athlete honors and over 150 Academic All-MAC honors.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>He led his team to back-to-back MAC semifinal appearances in 2023 and 2024, compiling a record of 22-15-5. 2023 included two first team All-MAC selections in Kelsey Salopek and Alisa Arthur. \u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>In 2021, Marinaro's Flashes returned to some of their best form, ending the season with a 13-5-3 record. They only lost one game in regular season MAC play. Eventually, the Flashes made it all the way to the MAC Championship. Their overtime performances were huge in their success, as they ended the season undefeated in overtime. Over the course of the season, the Flashes outscored their opponents 44-30. Forwards Cameron Shendenhelm and Karly Hellstrom made the All-MAC First Team, as did defender Tianna Harris. Harris was also named MAC Defensive Player of the Year. Freshman Flashes also stood out, as midfielders Siena Stambolich and Alisa Arthur and defender Grace Barresi were all named to the All-MAC Freshman Team. \u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>The 2020 season was moved to the spring of 2021 and was limited to a 10-game schedule of only MAC opponents. Three of those games were canceled. The Flashes went 2-1 in their remaining three home games. \u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>In 2019, the Flashes outshot their opponents and forced them into 117 saves over the course of the season. Three Flashes were recognized with All-MAC distinctions: midfielder Vital Kats (first team), forward Cameron Shedenhelm (second team) and defender Grace Wolber (freshman team). Kats was brilliant from midfield for the Flashes scoring 8 and assisting 8. Shedenhelm showed great all-around forward play, scoring 6 and assisting 6. \u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>The 2018 season saw the Golden Flashes reach the 10-win mark and qualify for the MAC Tournament for the eighth consecutive season and is the only MAC women’s soccer program to accomplish both feats during that stretch.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Under Marinaro's leadership, the 2017 team captured the program's third MAC regular season championship with a 9-2 league record and hosted the MAC Tournament’s final weekend for the second year in a row. Paige Culver was named a United Soccer Coaches All-American and MAC Defensive Player of the Year as the leader of a backline that matched the program record with 11 shutouts. Midfielder Vital Kats was the third Flash to earn MAC Freshman of the Year honors.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>The historic 2016 campaign included Kent State’s first NCAA Tournament appearance and program record 15 victories, which included a 13-match unbeaten streak. The Flashes posted an 8-1-2 conference record to win the MAC East Division crown and captured the program’s first MAC Tournament Championship with a 1-0 victory over Northern Illinois inside of Dix Stadium. Two-time MAC Offensive Player of the Year Jenna Hellstrom was named Kent State’s first ever NSCAA All-American after totaling a program record 38 points. Hellstrom headlined a record five All-MAC selections for the Flashes.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Kent State began its double-digit victory streak in 2011 with a MAC East title, marking the team’s first conference trophy since back-to-back first-place finishes in 2003 and 2004.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>After being promoted to head coach Jan. 1, 2001, Marinaro quickly moved Kent State to the top of the MAC, winning back-to-back MAC regular season championships in 2003 and 2004 when the program posted a combined 23-9-8 record. The Flashes posted a record-setting 11 shutouts in 2003 and earned a share of the MAC crown in 2004 by jumping from fourth place into a tie for first in the season’s final weekend.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>As an assistant coach on Colleen Marcum’s staff for the program’s first four years, Marinaro helped the Golden Flashes rebound from a difficult inaugural season to go a 31-24-2 over the next three years. His primary duties as an assistant included working with the goalkeepers and defense, as well as scouting and recruiting.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>A goalkeeper by trade, Marinaro spent five seasons (1993-97) playing with various teams in the National Professional Soccer League, finishing his professional career with the Cleveland Crunch. He also played for the Harrisburg Heat, Buffalo Blizzard and Chicago Power. He was selected to the NPSL All-Rookie Team in 1994 and was the runner-up for Rookie of the Year honors as a member of the Power. Marinaro first played professionally with the Toronto Blizzard of the American Professional Soccer League from 1992-93. His brother Hector, currently the men’s soccer coach at John Carroll University, is the all-time leader in points and goals in Major Indoor Soccer League (MISL) history.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>In addition, Marinaro served as a coach for the Ohio State North team for the Olympic Development Program and was a member of the ODP Region II staff. He also worked at the Cleveland Crunch Summer Camps in 1995 and 1996. Currently, he is the director of coaching for the Stow Soccer Club.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>A native of Toronto, Ontario, Marinaro received his master’s degree in sports administration from Kent State in the summer of 2001. He graduated from Clemson University in 1992 with a bachelor’s degree in language and international trade and was a member of the Tigers’ 1987 national championship team.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Marinaro currently holds a United States Soccer Federation National “B” Coaching License.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>He resides in Stow with his wife, Michele, and their son, She also earned a spot on the Division One OSCA All-Ohio Team and College Soccer Madness All-Conference Team.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Hellstrom graduated from Kent State in 2017 with a Bachelor's Soccer, Field Hockey, Softball, and Women’s Golf programs. Ashley advises her assigned student-athletes on course selection and registration, program requirements, and transfer credits, across various programs and colleges. Among other tasks she also partners with compliance sta? to certify continuing eligibility under NCAA and institutional standards and meets with prospective students and families on recruiting visits to further explain academic resources available and expectations at KSU.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Under Ashley’s guidance her programs and the department have seen various academic successes and milestones. She led Men’s Basketball to its highest term (Fall 2022, Fall 2024) and highest cumulative (Fall 2022, Fall 2023, Spring 2025) GPAs in program history, and to the NABC Honor Roll for the 2024-2025 Season (first time in program history). Ashley also led Women’s Soccer to their highest term and cumulative GPAs in program history (Fall 2024) and led Field Hockey to their highest term GPAs in program history (Fall 2024) and highest academic year GPA in the MAC (24-25). While a part of the academic support staff, Kent State student-athletes have collectively set new records for highest term and cumulative department GPA in recorded history (Fall 2022, Spring 2023, Fall 2023, Fall 2024, and Spring 2025).\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>In addition to her role in Academics, Ashley serves as ESPN+ Color Analyst for all home and select away Kent State Men’s Basketball games showcasing her knowledge as a former head coach.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Prior to her time at Kent State, Ashley served as Head Women’s Basketball Coach at Clarion University from June 2014 to August 2022. Under her leadership the Golden Eagles saw a 13-win Improvement from her first year to her fourth year. In 2018-2019 they recorded the longest winning streak to begin a season since 2004. Ashley also achieved the program’s longest program win streak since 2004-2005, the first overall winning record for the program since 2009-2010, and the most conference wins and first winning conference record since 2007-2008 (16-17).\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Before Clarion, Ashley served as Assistant Women’s Basketball Coach for three prior programs including Iona College from June 2013 to April 2014, George Mason University from April 2008 to June 2013, and her graduate alma mater Radford University from July 2005 to April 2008.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>A student-athlete herself, Ashley attended the University of North Alabama graduating in 2002.
